A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COG research work. Their main text, equations, figures, four tables and appendices A–H are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V2 reports original interpolation and centroid benchmarks, normality-testing experiments, simulations and qualitative image and point-cloud results.

after.justification: V4 retains those original results and adds diagnostic analyses, including the seed–interpolant correlations in Figure 8.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same COG affine correction, interpolation and centroid weights, and QR/pseudoinverse subspace construction. Revised notation and normality-analysis explanations do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover ImageNet1k inversion, interpolation and centroid determination; synthetic normality failure cases; image subspaces; ShapeNet point-cloud subspaces; and unconditional interpolation. The revised diagnostics remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: The interpolation, centroid and normality-test comparator sets remain unchanged in Tables 1–4. The without-COG control displayed in v4 Figure 2 already appeared in the corresponding v2 appendix analysis; it is not a newly evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: V4 Figure 5 pools inversion budgets and compares interpolation quality between p-value groups among seeds with LPIPS reconstruction error below 0.05. V2 instead reports accepted/rejected groups by inversion budget. This adds a reconstruction-quality control, while the main benchmark protocol in Appendix E remains unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 extends the existing normality analysis with reconstruction-error-conditioned interpolation comparisons and Figure 8's quantitative examination of whether interpolants inherit low seed p-values. Existing failure-vector tests, inversion-budget analyses, FID-setting comparisons and large-centroid failure examples remain.

E5.justification: V2 Figures 4–5 show medians and intervals described as 50% and 95% confidence intervals. V4 Figure 4 uses individual observations and 10th/50th/90th percentiles; Figure 5 replaces its intervals with quality proportions. Figure 8 adds Pearson correlation estimates. The 10,000-sample procedures in Appendices B and D are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results, including COG's 67.4% accuracy and 38.9 FID for interpolation. V4 Figure 8 newly reports correlations of 0.79 for acceptance indicators and 0.66 for log10 p-values. Figures 4–5 replace diagnostic summaries and examples, and Figure 2 omits one previous subspace slice. These changes do not establish a benchmark performance gain.

T1.justification: The Gaussian-combination derivations, assumptions and five lemmas with proofs in Appendices A–C are retained, including the SLERP approximation and subspace-weight arguments. Equation renumbering and revised time/latent notation do not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: Both versions claim Gaussian-preserving linear combinations, inexpensive architecture-independent interpolation and subspace construction, and useful normality diagnostics. V4 foregrounds general linear combinations in the abstract, but that scope was already explicit in v2. The contribution list and conclusion retain their meaning.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 shifts from broad predictive language to an association between low p-values and poorer interpolants even among reconstructing seeds. It also adds a misleading explanation of p-values as probabilities of observing latent vectors. Sections 5.1 and G soften 'outperforms' to 'outperforms or maintains'; existing applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: V4 explicitly specifies 999 generation steps for Figures 4–5 and clarifies that Table 4 uses one step for both inversion and generation. V2 does not clearly document the former and only alludes to the latter. These disclosures do not independently establish changed execution settings; other implementation and access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning remain the same. Changing Samuel et al.'s year from 2024 to 2023 and correcting the Kolmogorov author entry are bibliographic repairs, not additions or changes of prior work.

P1.justification: V4 revises the abstract and Section 3.2 narrative, regularizes latent/time notation, and edits explanations and captions. These are localized revisions; the overall section sequence and appendix organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The central diagnostic visuals are substantially redesigned: Figures 4–5 replace interval summaries and reconstruction mosaics with observation-level plots, a quality histogram and new examples; Figure 8 adds correlation plots. Figure 2 juxtaposes a retained COG slice with the existing appendix control. Most other figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The reconstruction-quality control in Figure 5 and new correlation evidence in Figure 8 modestly strengthen the normality argument, while explicit generation settings improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh the loss of budget-stratified Q-Align intervals and the misleading new p-value explanation in Section 3.2. The method, proofs and main benchmark evidence remain unchanged, limiting the overall improvement.
